function: Meta-DDPG jointly sets BS receive beamforming, user power, transmission and reflection beamforming of multiple active STAR-RISs, and user-STAR-RIS association to maximize uplink sum rate (p. 1-3).
system: Uplink NOMA: BS with 4 antennas, 16 single-antenna users, N=4 active STAR-RISs (simultaneously transmitting and reflecting, with second-order reflections); Rayleigh channels; frequency band not stated (p. 1-2, 4-5).
method: Meta-DDPG: deep deterministic policy gradient (actor-critic reinforcement learning) with a meta-learning loss (bi-level optimization); 5000 episodes, replay buffer 10^4 (p. 3-5).
data_channel: Own simulation with Rayleigh fading channels and the Table I parameters; no standardized channel model, public dataset, or measurements (p. 4-5).
test_conditions: No separate test stage described; learning curves over 5000 episodes and total rate versus Pmax, number of STAR-RIS elements, and users, same simulated environment (p. 4-6).
baselines: Non-learned: convex optimization approach for multi-active STAR-RIS (Fig. 4); learned: DDPG without the meta module; system variants: multi STAR-RIS, single-active STAR-RIS, single reflection (p. 4-5).
metrics: Reward and total sum rate versus episodes, Pmax, and number of elements; percent gains (19% over DDPG, 74.1% for second-order reflections); complexity (p. 4-6).
complexity: FLOPS-based time-complexity expressions for the actor, critic, and meta-critic networks (Eqs. 18-19); Meta-DDPG costs 2.46% more than DDPG; convex benchmark complexity expression given (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "in Rayleigh fading channels are detailed in Table I". Custom simulator with a textbook fading model; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "it offers significantly better adaptability". Claimed only; Figs. 2-5 (p. 6) show learning curves and sweeps of Pmax, elements, and users in one environment, with no test in conditions unseen in training and no adaptation experiment.
q3_support: p. 4: "algorithm consistently outperforms the DDPG algorithm with 19% improvement"; p. 5: "a comparison between the Meta-DDPG algorithm and the convex approach". DDPG is the proposed method without its meta module (an ablation); no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "While Meta-DDPG algorithm increases complexity by 2.46% compared to DDPG". Section IV-B gives the complexity expressions of Eqs. (18) and (19), and p. 5 gives the convex benchmark complexity.
q5_support: p. 4: "in Rayleigh fading channels are detailed in Table I". Parameters only; the data are simulated and no code or data link appears in the 6 pages.
notes: Area 3 (beamforming and STAR-RIS configuration, learned jointly with power and association). Borderline q3: the non-learned convex benchmark is compared, but the only learned baseline is DDPG, which is Meta-DDPG without its meta module (ablation); if the reviewer counts DDPG as a standard algorithm on the same problem, q3 becomes 1. No experiment tests the adaptability claimed on p. 4, so q2 stays 0. The PDF is the arXiv:2401.07100v3 preprint (p. 1) and prints no DOI; its title and letter format agree with the DOI.
